subject: ela
intro: Words connect to each other in interesting ways. Sometimes writers use figurative language, words that do not mean exactly what they say. "It is raining cats and dogs" does not mean animals are falling, it means it is raining hard. That is nonliteral. When words mean exactly what they say, that is literal. Related words can also show shades of meaning, small differences in how strong an idea is, like cool, cold, then freezing. And words connect to real life, like the word cozy fitting a warm blanket. In this lesson you will practice telling literal from figurative, seeing how words connect to real life, and putting related words in order.

items.prompt:
Is the underlined phrase literal or figurative? Explain what it really means.

When Grandma said the leftover pizza was gone, Marco was so hungry he could eat a horse.

What does "could eat a horse" really mean?

steps: Ask if the words are exactly true. Marco cannot really eat a whole horse.
So the phrase is figurative, not literal.
It is a fun way to say he is extremely hungry.
The real meaning is that he is very, very hungry.
solution.answer: It is figurative. "Could eat a horse" means Marco is extremely hungry, not that he would really eat a horse.

items.prompt:
Put these related words in order from least to most, and explain the shades of meaning.

cold, cool, freezing

Which word shows the smallest amount and which shows the most?

steps: All three words are about low temperature, but they are not equal.
Cool is only a little low.
Cold is lower than cool.
Freezing is the most, so cold enough to freeze.
solution.answer: From least to most: cool, cold, freezing. "Cool" shows the smallest amount of cold and "freezing" shows the most.

items.prompt:
Connect the word to real life.

The word "delicious" describes food that tastes very good.

Name a food that could be called delicious, and explain why the word fits.

steps: "Delicious" means tasting very good.
Think of a food most people enjoy the taste of, such as warm chocolate cake.
The word fits because the cake tastes very good.
Connecting a word to a real example helps you remember its meaning.
solution.answer: A warm slice of chocolate cake could be called delicious because it tastes very good, which is what "delicious" means.

items.prompt:
These three words are related but show shades of meaning. Order them from least sure to most sure.

knew, believed, suspected

Explain your order.

steps: All three words are about how sure a person is.
"Suspected" means you have only a small guess.
"Believed" means you feel fairly sure but are not certain.
"Knew" means you are completely sure it is true.
solution.answer: From least sure to most sure: suspected, believed, knew. "Suspected" is just a guess, "believed" is fairly sure, and "knew" is completely sure.

items.prompt:
Is the underlined phrase literal or figurative? Explain what it really means.

After the long test, Dev said his brain was fried.

What does "his brain was fried" really mean?

steps: Ask if the words are exactly true. Dev's brain is not really cooked.
So the phrase is figurative.
It is a way to say his mind is very tired.
The real meaning is that he is worn out from thinking so hard.
solution.answer: It is figurative. "His brain was fried" means Dev was very tired from thinking hard, not that his brain was really cooked.

items.prompt:
Put these related words in order from least to most, and explain.

happy, joyful, glad

Which word shows the strongest happy feeling?

steps: All three words describe a happy feeling.
"Glad" is a small, gentle happy feeling.
"Happy" is a bit stronger.
"Joyful" is the strongest, full of joy.
solution.answer: From least to most: glad, happy, joyful. "Joyful" shows the strongest happy feeling.

items.prompt:
Connect the word to real life.

Someone who is "generous" likes to share and give to others.

Describe a real situation that shows a generous person, and explain why the word fits.

steps: "Generous" means willing to share and give.
Think of an action that shows sharing, such as giving half your snack to a friend who forgot lunch.
The word fits because the person is giving to help someone else.
Connecting the word to a real action shows you understand it.
solution.answer: A child who gives half of her lunch to a friend who forgot food is generous, because "generous" means willing to share and give to others.

items.prompt:
Is the underlined phrase literal or figurative? Explain.

The classroom was so quiet during the test that you could hear a pin drop.

What does "you could hear a pin drop" really mean?

steps: Ask if the words are exactly true. The point is not really about a pin.
So the phrase is figurative.
A dropped pin makes almost no sound, so hearing it means it is extremely quiet.
The real meaning is that the room was very, very quiet.
solution.answer: It is figurative. "You could hear a pin drop" means the room was extremely quiet, so quiet that even a tiny sound would be heard.

items.prompt:
Order these related words from least to most, then use one in a sentence.

like, love, adore

Explain your order.

steps: All three words are about how much you enjoy something.
"Like" is the gentlest feeling.
"Love" is stronger than like.
"Adore" is the strongest, loving something very much.
solution.answer: From least to most: like, love, adore. Sample sentence: I adore my grandmother's stories, because I love hearing them more than anything.

items.prompt:
Decide if the sentence uses literal or figurative language. Then rewrite the meaning in your own plain words.

When the teacher announced a surprise party, the news spread like wildfire.

Is "spread like wildfire" literal or figurative, and what does it mean?

steps: Ask if the words are exactly true. The news is not really fire.
So the phrase is figurative.
Wildfire spreads very fast, so the phrase compares the news to that speed.
The plain meaning is that the news traveled very quickly.
solution.answer: It is figurative. "Spread like wildfire" means the news traveled very quickly from person to person, not that there was a real fire.
